Embedding in your app: the agent-token exchange, seats and caps ​

Settled design from a production integration (a mobile app hosting the widget in a web view with native bridges for photos and voice). Built into packages/gateway/src/auth.ts.

Principles ​

  1. Your app authenticates the user against your auth service. Nothing in the SDK or the gateway logs a user in.
  2. Your broad access token never enters a web view. The native side exchanges it for a short-lived AGENT TOKEN that only the agent API accepts.
  3. Identity is verified once, at exchange, by calling your auth service — and fails closed.
  4. A seat is checked at exchange and a cap is enforced before every turn.
  5. A session id is an id, not a credential. Every session endpoint checks the owner.

The three credentials ​

CredentialHeld byLifetimeGoes to
Your access token (+ refresh)the native app onlyyoursPOST /api/auth/exchange only
App key (X-Agent-App-Key)the app build (one per platform/tenant)until rotatedevery gateway call; an identifier, not a secret
Agent tokenthe web view's JS memory + the native side15 min, renewed by the native sideevery /api/* call

Flow ​

user ──login──▶ your auth service ──▶ access token held by the app
app  ── POST /api/auth/exchange [X-Agent-App-Key, Bearer <access token>] ──▶ gateway
gateway: app key → tenant ; GET AGENT_AUTH_VERIFY_URL (strict) → sub, name, firm ;
         GET AGENT_ENTITLEMENT_URL/{firm}/{sub} → seat + cap ; vault the access token ;
         mint {sub, firm_id, tenant, seat, jti, exp}
app  ◀── { agent_token, expires_in: 900, user, firm, seat, cap } ──
web view ── widget calls opts.token() (async) → agent token ──▶ every /api/* call
gateway: verify signature, exp, jti not revoked → bind the session's owner = sub →
         per tool call, attach the VAULTED access token (acts as the user; your API enforces permissions)
app: re-exchange at expires_in − 60 s, or on 401 token_expired, with a fresh access token

Endpoints ​

  • POST /api/auth/exchange → 200 {agent_token, expires_in, user, firm, seat, cap}; 401 invalid_token / invalid_app_key; 403 no_seat (seat: none|suspended) / firm_inactive; 503 auth_unavailable / entitlement_unavailable. Disabled (501) without AGENT_TOKEN_SECRET.
  • POST /api/auth/logout — revokes the jti, drops the vaulted token.
  • A removed user keeps chatting for at most the token's lifetime; wire your admin backend to revoke on removal (revokeUser) for immediate effect.

Entitlement contract ​

GET AGENT_ENTITLEMENT_URL/{firm_id}/{sub} with AGENT_ENTITLEMENT_KEY →

json
{ "seat": "active|none|suspended", "plan": "pro",
  "cap": { "credits": 400, "period": "month", "resets_at": "2026-11-01T00:00:00+05:30" },
  "firm_status": "active|past_due" }

Decided defaults: unseated users are refused at exchange (no trial); caps per seat per calendar month with a daily ceiling of 10% of the month; the user sees a percent; over cap ⇒ 429 usage_cap with scope and resets_at. Account identity for metering: account_id = <tenant>:<sub>, parent = firm — opaque, so it can move to another identity platform.

Expiry mid-turn ​

If your API answers 401 inside a turn, the gateway ends the turn with token_expired, retryable: true; the native side re-exchanges and the client resends the message once. Reads are harmless; the one write is idempotent (session + draft fingerprint).

The web-view host (what the first integration measured) ​

A web-view host of the widget was GO on Android: tap-to-interactive 0.7–0.9 s in a warm process, ~2.6 s on a first-ever web view in an install, +80–90 MB; keep the widget script compressed and versioned, give the host page a CSP and a navigation allowlist, and bridge photo picking and the microphone natively. The widget's opts.token accepts an async function so a renewed token applies on the next request.
